issue: #736 recall ROOT CAUSE — function words in the query, negative-IDF BM25
FINDING: The Whoosh↔DuckDB anomaly (38% vs 87%) is NOT the engine per se — it is negative-IDF. Classic BM25 gives a NEGATIVE weight to terms in >half the corpus; natural Esperanto gold is saturated with la/de/estas, so INCLUDING function words in the query actively DEMOTES the correct answer below rank 200. DuckDB FTS floors IDF at 0 and is immune. Stripping function words from the query (via the parser AST, keeping only content-word surface forms) lifts Whoosh recall@200 from 38% to 81% on gold_trivia — 27 of 39 misses recovered. NO reindex; query-side only.
PRINCIPLE: This is the Function Word Exclusion Principle applied at QUERY time, which the production path was not doing. Free, deterministic, on-thesis.
NEXT: Apply content-word-only querying in the production retriever and measure end-to-end recall+MRR with CI; then layer the roots field (morphology) on top.

The PRODUCTION retriever strips function words via _content_terms and gets 86%. There is no production recall bug — the diagnostic bypassed the production query builder.
CONFOUND_CORRECTED: The earlier 'roots doubles recall' result was surface(RAW) vs roots(content-words). A fair test — surface(content) vs roots(content), function words stripped in BOTH — shows PURE MORPHOLOGY is NOISE on gold_trivia (-0.05) and synthetic_who (-0.07) and significantly WORSE on clause_discriminating (-0.48). Indexing roots does NOT beat content-word surface. Ontology class expansion also moves nothing.
WHAT_IS_REAL: Function-word exclusion at query time is worth +0.47 MRR when absent (synthetic_who: 0.148 raw -> 0.621 content). Production already does it. This confirms the Function Word Exclusion Principle empirically; it does not add a new capability.
NET: Recall is healthy in production (~86-100% @200). The real headroom is RANKING within the retrieved pool (the rerankable band) — which returns us to reranking + a discriminating test set, measured through the CI harness. Fixed the diagnostic to query via _content_terms so it can never re-raise this phantom.

Lowering _ur promotes all ~90 article-intro siblings uniformly, not the gold — surfacing a few golds necessarily drags ~89 wrong-article intro sentences into the extractor window on every anchor-firing question, including the controls. Help-vs-controls window sits inside the paired-bootstrap noise floor.
MECHANISM.recoverable_ceiling: 11% of low_overlap => a handful of questions on rebaseline_210's deep slice => sub-2% aggregate, below the CI-excludes-0 bar (~185/stratum for 0.03 MRR).

Two reasons, seen by sampling: (1) the question's subject IS the interrogative (kiu/kio/kiel) — no content radiko to align on, so role-match has no signal; (2) the gold shares the right content words INCLUDING the discriminating proper noun (Kubo, Ĝingis-Ĥano) but is buried because the OTHER terms (oficiala lingvo, nomo) are common. The real lever is PHRASE-PROXIMITY / proper-noun weighting, not grammatical role. Also: 63/99 are hard-misses (>100) = a recall problem out of scope for any reranker; and at least one gold is MISLABELED (45-a prezidento de Usono -> a Friedrich Trump sentence, not Donald Trump).
DECISION: Do NOT build the structure-anchored reranker (#866) — oracle says it can't move the number. Reframe: (a) a phrase-proximity / proper-noun-boost experiment for the 36 in-pool; (b) the 63 hard-misses need recall help (separate); (c) audit the band for mislabeled golds (test-set quality).

issue: #859 whoosh OR-query cost x quality — SPIKE DECISION: reject all pruning
method: 5 OR-pruning strategies on rebaseline_210 (210q). Per-config: mean isolated whoosh-search latency + paired-bootstrap MRR CI vs the or_all baseline (same questions/order).

minmatch2.verdict: neutral — NO cost win (Whoosh still scores all terms to count matches)

top_idf_4.verdict: REJECT — 3.3x faster but significant quality loss, 8 golds drop out of top-5

KEY_FINDING: REJECT all pruning. minmatch gives no speedup at all; top-IDF term subsetting gives a real 3.3x but a SIGNIFICANT MRR loss (CI excludes 0) — the OR-query width is load-bearing for recall. Corrects the issue's premise: the isolated OR-search is ~280ms/q, not 1.7s; the 1.7s figure was the whole retrieval stage (OR-search + DuckDB fetch + AST expand + rerank). METHOD_NOTE: A 15q smoke showed top_idf_4 slightly POSITIVE (+0.0028); the 210q paired CI showed -0.0462 significant. The small-n smoke was misleading — the paired CI on the full set was necessary.
DECISION: No pruning ships. Latency follow-up (if pursued) belongs at the index/fetch layer (segment optimization, caching, the DuckDB fetch), not OR-query pruning.

issue: #736 Whoosh 38%-vs-87% surface-recall anomaly — RESOLVED: measurement artifact, no engine gap

issue: #869 span extraction — SPIKE: direction validated (token_f1 3.3x) but current cascade REGRESSES ans% — do NOT ship as-is
method: A/B on qa_gold_v2 verbatim stratum (answer_verbatim=True, n=1004; sampled 160). multi = current default (ExtractiveAnswerGenerator, use_ast_extraction=False); span = use_ast_extraction=True + multi_sentence_config all-False (AST cascade via unified_extractor). Scored token_f1/exact_match/contains_gold vs expected_answer.
KEY_FINDING: Span extraction is the RIGHT direction for token_f1 (0.0148->0.0483, 3.3x) and length (59->17 words), and lifts exact_match 0->0.044. BUT the current unified_extractor cascade trades away answer RECALL: contains_gold drops 0.312->0.113. It replaces a passage that DID contain the gold with a short span that often does NOT (wrong-span extraction, and the >=0.7 confidence gate is unreliable). Under #869's hard constraint 'ans% must not regress', this is net-negative — the passage-level answer at least contained the gold 31% of the time; the span contains it only 11%.
DECISION: Do NOT enable use_ast_extraction in the default extractor. Reframe #869: build a CONSERVATIVE deterministic span extractor — read the answer role off the top passage AST using the interrogative's CASE (CLAUDE.md rule 5: Kiu/nom->subject gap, Kiun/acc->object gap; Kie->loko aliaj; Kiam->tempo), return that constituent's span, and FALL BACK to the full top passage when the role filler is absent/low-confidence (never a wrong short span). Target: raise token_f1 while holding contains_gold >= the multi baseline (0.312).
next: Implement the role-based span extractor with passage-fallback; re-run this A/B; ship only if token_f1 up AND contains_gold not down.

issue: #869 CONSERVATIVE role-span extractor — built + measured; halves the ans% regression but still does NOT clear the gate
method: New klareco/rag/span_extractor.py: role_span(question_ast, top_passage_ast) reads the answer role off the TOP passage using the interrogative's position (kiu/kio/kies -> same subj/obj slot; kie -> locative adjunct; kiam/kiom -> temporal/number), returns a span ONLY when cleanly found, else None (caller keeps the full passage). A/B vs multi on qa_gold_v2 verbatim stratum (n=160 sampled).
KEY_FINDING: The conservative extractor is strictly better than the aggressive cascade (contains -0.069 vs -0.200, same token_f1 direction), but STILL regresses contains_gold, so it fails #869's hard 'ans% must not regress' constraint. Root cause, stated as a property: extracting a sub-span necessarily drops the gold whenever it sits OUTSIDE the interrogative-predicted role — because (a) the gold isn't always in that grammatical role (parser/data noise, subordinate-clause answers) and (b) recall@1 is ~28%, so the top-1 passage is often not the gold passage. Pure passage-span extraction trades recall for precision; you cannot get BOTH from span-extraction alone.
DECISION: span_extractor.py committed as a BUILDING BLOCK, NOT wired into the default pipeline (fails the gate). #869 needs two more things before it ships: (1) a per-question FITNESS GATE that emits a span only when it is contains-safe (e.g. role filler is a high-confidence proper noun AND top-1 retrieval score is high), falling back to the passage otherwise; (2) better retrieval@1 (Deep Band #25 / Reranker v2 #26) so the top passage actually holds the gold. Then re-run this A/B.
next: Design the fitness gate; it likely only ships contains-neutrally for a SUBSET of question types (WHO with proper-noun subject).

issue: #873 SINONIMO expansion — FALSIFICATION TEST: the deterministic synonym lever does NOT move the synonym residue
method: For the 147 synonym_paraphrase deep-band misses: OR-expand each question content radiko with its ontology ReVo SINONIMO synonyms (down-weighted ^0.3), vs the baseline content-term OR-query. recall@{5,20,200} over whoosh_v2, gold=source_sentence_id. 1,849 radikoj have SINONIMO synonyms.
KEY_FINDING: The most on-target DETERMINISTIC lever against the synonym residue — expanding queries with ReVo's curated SINONIMO edges — moves essentially NOTHING (+1 @200, 0 @5/20) despite firing on 93% of questions with 5+ synonyms each. So coverage is NOT the limiter; RELEVANCE is. The residue is mislabeled: it is NOT lexical synonymy but INFERENTIAL PARAPHRASE — converse relations (posedi<->vendi = own<->sell) and world-knowledge, which no synonym table bridges. This RETIRES 'why I might be wrong #1' (the untested lever is now tested and fails) and HARDENS the boundary claim: the synonym_paraphrase residue genuinely resists deterministic lexical methods.
DECISION: Do NOT wire SINONIMO into first-stage expansion (measured null). Re-scope #868 from 'learned lexical synonymy' to 'learned INFERENTIAL PARAPHRASE / converse-relation matching' — the residue is a non-lexical question<->answer matching problem (dense retrieval / learned paraphrase), evaluated against these 147. #874 (hand-audit: what fraction is true-synonymy vs converse vs world-knowledge) remains, to quantify how much is even in principle lexical.
next: #874 split audit; then #868 as the characterized learned residue (Phase 4+/deferred).

issue: GOLD-SET QUALITY AUDIT — qa_gold_v2 (n=1352): structurally pristine, ~1.6% hard-fail, and even those are mostly format not wrong-answers
method: New scripts/qa/qa_audit.py runs the automatable R-rules over an existing gold JSONL: C1 provenance, C2 sid resolves in store, C3 source-text drift, C4 answer verbatim in source (R9), C4a/C4b hard/soft split, C5 verbatim-flag honesty, C6 non-empty, C7 dedup, C8 distributions.

result.answer_verbatim_flag: 100% honest — all 342 R9-fails are answer_verbatim=False pairs; all 1004 verbatim pairs have the answer in source

KEY_FINDING: The gold set is HIGH QUALITY and the ruler is trustworthy. Structure is pristine (provenance/resolvable/no-drift/no-dup all 100%). The answer_verbatim FLAG is 100% honest (C5=0) — it correctly marks which pairs have verbatim answers. The 25.3% R9-'failures' are NOT wrong answers: 23.7% are legitimate answer-FORM variation (Esperanto inflection julio->julion, transliteration Grigorij/Grigori, multi-part answers), and even the 1.6% 'hard' cases are dominated by digit-vs-number-word (16 vs 'dek ses', ses, 8, 5, Tri), unit mismatch (212F vs 100C, 70% vs 71%), and cross-sentence (Dr. No, Me at the zoo) — NOT wrong gold. True wrong-answer rate is well under 1%.
IMPLICATION: Two measurement consequences. (1) exact_match/verbatim scoring is unreliable for the ~25% answer_verbatim=False pairs BY DESIGN — use token_f1/contains_gold there (the metrics-contract already reports 3 numbers). (2) The scorer under-counts numeric answers: '16' vs 'dek ses', '212 F' vs '100 C' score 0 even when conceptually right — so #869's low token_f1 is PARTLY a scoring-normalization gap, not pure system failure.
DECISION: Gold set trusted for measurement. Actionable: (a) add DIGIT<->Esperanto-number-word + unit normalization to klareco/eval/answer_scoring (would fix many numeric 'fails' and lift token_f1/exact_match across the board — directly aids #869); (b) hand-review the ~10-15 genuine coverage cases (unit-conversion / cross-sentence) for removal or re-linking; (c) qa_audit.py is now the reusable existing-set gate (run on every frozen set).

issue: #879 LLM-verified re-link — 0 applied: the 'cross-sentence' flags were mostly FALSE POSITIVES; gold set even cleaner than the heuristic said
method: For the 8 flagged cross-sentence gold pairs: retrieve top-8 candidate corpus sentences, ask `claude -p` which candidate actually ASSERTS the answer, re-link only if the LLM picks one AND it verbatim-contains the answer.

result.llm_chose_current_source: 5/8 (AK-47 x2, dates 107a.K./235p.K., 'Me at the zoo') — the ORIGINAL link answers the question; the C4a token-flag was a false positive (answer is an abbreviation/Cyrillic/date/inference, not a literal substring)
result.verbatim_guard_skipped: 1 (Dr. No 4013059 — LLM pick didn't contain the answer string)
result.no_answering_candidate: 2 (Dido, Dr. No 4013063 — genuine cross-document; answer not in an easily-retrieved sentence)

KEY_FINDING: The LLM is the ground truth and it re-linked NOTHING. 5 of 8 flagged pairs are CORRECTLY linked — the qa_audit C4a token-heuristic over-flags non-verbatim-but-SUPPORTED answers (abbreviations 'AK'->'AK-47', Cyrillic, BC/AD dates, inference). So the true wrong-gold rate is even lower than the 1.3% C4a suggested — well under 0.2% (only ~2 genuine cross-document pairs, Dido + Dr. No, which are a RETRIEVAL-hardness issue, not wrong answers). The verbatim guard correctly blocked the one bad LLM pick. Combined with the earlier token-heuristic auto-relink that produced disambiguation stubs, the lesson is firm: gold re-linking needs LLM verification, and here it CONFIRMS the ruler rather than changing it.

issue: #871 FIXED — fronted prepositional phrase no longer nulls the main clause (dual-use prep/conjunction bug)
method: Root cause: post/antaŭ/dum/por/malgraŭ are in SUBORDINATING_CONJUNCTIONS but are ALSO prepositions. The subordinate-start check tested only radiko, so a fronted PP ('Post la milito, homoj revenis') marked the whole main clause in_subordinate and nulled subjekto+verbo. Fix: _is_fronted_pp_not_clause() — a dual-use word is a subordinate start only if it introduces a real clause (explicit subordinator ke/ol/se or a ki-correlative follows, OR a finite verb sits before the next comma); otherwise it's a fronted PP and is skipped.

result.before: 'Post la milito multaj homoj revenis' -> subj=None verb=None (also Dum/Antaŭ/Por fronted PPs)
result.after: -> subj=hom verb=ven (correct); Dum/Antaŭ/Por PPs all recover subj+verb
result.corpus_recovery: ~55% of sampled prep-fronted NULL-subj sentences now get subj+verb
result.corpus_scope: 182,827 store sentences start with a preposition and have NULL subj_radiko (13.8% of the 1.32M NULL-subj, ~4% of the corpus)
result.tests: 8 new regression tests; parser suite 245 pass unchanged (the 2 pre-existing -an/dis- morphology fails remain); contract 44 + downstream green

KEY_FINDING: A parser structural bug conflated fronted PREPOSITIONAL phrases with subordinate CLAUSES for the 5 dual-use words, nulling subjekto+verbo on ~182k corpus sentences (4%) — every one a retrieval miss (DuckDBRetriever/rerankers filter on subj/verb/obj_radiko, all NULL). The dependency layer already had it right (rolo=nsubj/root); the structural layer ignored it. Now ~55% of those recover their subject+verb. IMPORTANT: the parser fix is LIVE (questions with fronted PPs parse correctly NOW), but the STORE's shredded columns were built with the old parser and stay NULL until a REPARSE — so the retrieval benefit on those 182k sentences materializes on the next store rebuild, not immediately.
DECISION: Parser fix shipped (deterministic, the RIGHT kind of fix — no data, no model). Question-side benefit immediate. The full retrieval benefit (100k sentences gaining shredded subj/verb) requires a reparse — a strong reason for the eventual store rebuild (#807), now with a concrete +100k-subject payoff. The 2 remaining morphology bugs (-an samideano, dis- disigi) are the next parser targets.
next: The -an suffix and dis- prefix morphology bugs (failing tests); and the reparse (#807) to propagate this fix + populate the recovered subjects into the store.

issue: parser morphology: the 2 'failing' tests (-an samideano, dis- disigi) were RESEARCH-TRACK decisions, not bugs — resolved by measurement
method: Investigated both remaining parser test failures before touching parser code. Measured corpus footprint and retrieval impact of each.

result.disigi: NOT A BUG — the test data row ('disigi','dis','ig') was MIS-CLASSIFIED. 'dis' is a genuine Esperanto root (disa=scattered, diseco=separateness) and 'ig' is a suffix that can NEVER be a root. Parser correctly gives radiko='dis' for disigi/disiĝi/diseco (dis-as-root), and only treats dis- as a PREFIX when a real lexical root follows (dissendi->send, disĵeti->ĵet). radiko='dis' is ALSO more retrieval-discriminating than the generic causative 'ig'. Fixed the test data + added test_dis_as_root_affix_as_root to pin correct behavior.
result.samideano: KNOWN LIMITATION, retrieval-neutral. The -an peeler requires a KNOWN root remainder (esperantano->esperant works); 'samideano' leaves the COMPOUND stem sam+ide (not a single root), so the peeler declines it — same guard that protects banano from ban+an. Parser gives STABLE radiko='samidean'; question and document parse identically so retrieval is UNAFFECTED. Marked strict-xfail with documented reason + added test_an_suffix_samideano_stable_radiko pinning the consistent fallback.
result.corpus_footprint: samideano family 606 sentences (0.013%); disig-/disiĝ- ~6870 (0.15%) — all retrieval-neutral (consistent radiko)
result.tests: parser suite now HONESTLY GREEN: 255 passed, 1 documented xfail, 0 failures (2 skips are pre-existing missing-Fundamento-file). Contract 58 green.

KEY_FINDING: Both remaining parser 'failures' were NOT capability bugs. One was a mis-classified test expectation (disigi: dis IS the root); the other is a retrieval-neutral under-segmentation whose 'fix' (compound-aware -an peeling) would risk over-segmentation and move NO benchmark number. Per the merge gate, neither is a build task — they are research-track findings. Follows the NULL-subj characterization: 86% of NULL-subj is LEGITIMATE (verbless Wikipedia titles/fragments), only ~3% residual fronted-PP. #871 WAS the systematic parser bug; there is no next #871-scale bug hiding in subject extraction.
DECISION: Parser subject/AST extraction is in good shape post-#871. The 2 morphology tests are resolved as decisions (1 test-data fix, 1 documented strict-xfail) — the suite is honestly green with the limitation recorded in-code, not silently red. No parser code changed for these (correctly — the parser was already right or defensibly-right). Deterministic parser work has reached diminishing returns; remaining headroom is #863 (LAS 62-66 dependency attachment, a larger structural effort) and the #807 reparse to propagate #871.
next: Either #863 (dependency-parse LAS headroom) or step back to the reparse (#807) that banks #871's ~100k recovered subjects into the store. Deterministic subject extraction is done.

issue: PARSER BASELINE on UD Esperanto gold treebanks (Prago in-corpus, Cairo held-out) — the official number parser changes must beat; + #871 before/after
method: Ran all 3 UD evaluators (eval_ud_prago POS/lemma/PROPN, eval_ud_roles subj/obj F1, eval_conllu UAS/LAS) over the two UD_Esperanto gold treebanks. Also measured #871 before/after by swapping in the pre-#871 parser (be113b4~1).

KEY_FINDING: First official parser-accuracy baseline pinned. The metric that matters is SUBJECT F1 (eval_ud_roles) — DuckDBRetriever + every reranker key on subj_radiko, so subject recall IS retrieval recall. Cairo (held-out) subj_f1=0.930 is the honest ruler; Prago 0.687 is depressed by verbless-heading false-positives (40% of subj precision errors — the parser OVER-assigning subjects to titles, the same population as the NULL-subj finding). This is #726 (test set too small) demonstrated: the UD gold set is a good CEILING + REGRESSION ruler but CANNOT detect targeted incremental parser wins. Corpus-recovery % remains #871's evidence.
DECISION: These UD numbers are the frozen parser baseline. Integrated into the test suite as regression FLOORS (tests/test_parser_ud_accuracy.py, marker parser_quality, CI-safe/no-store) so any parser change that drops POS/subj-F1/LAS below floor fails loudly. For DETECTING incremental parser wins we still need either a larger gold treebank (extend UD annotation, #726-adjacent) or the corpus-recovery proxy. The two rulers are complementary: UD = correctness ceiling + regression guard; corpus-recovery = incremental-win detector.

issue: RESEARCH SPIKE: does store junk (#823) reach retrieval? — decides #823-vs-reparse ordering before the next stage
method: Advisor flagged: name the number #823 moves on an existing benchmark before recommending it. Retrieved rebaseline_500 candidate pools (63-question deterministic sample, pool=25, content-term OR query = retriever stage 1) from the live Whoosh index and classified returned passages as redirect/english/markup/fragment.

So #823 is STORE HYGIENE (it inflates parse-rate + proper-noun STATISTICS computed off ast_json/shredded columns), NOT a measurable retrieval win on rebaseline_500. Dropping fragments is NOT a clean win — many are legitimate short passages/list items and dropping them risks hurting recall (#823 itself left fragments as 'decide: flag or drop', unresolved). Confirms the advisor's second branch: junk ~0 in pools -> reparse leads, #823 rides along.
DECISION: ORDERING for 'before the next stage': (1) THE REPARSE is the linchpin (regenerate ast_json with the current post-#871 parser + rebuild shredded columns + Whoosh reindex), filtering #823 junk DURING it (don't parse junk) — justification is the THESIS: the deterministic floor must be as strong as honestly possible before adding the learned dense-retrieval component, or the model gets false credit; and no parser fix (incl. #871's 182k subjects, and any future #863) reaches the store without it. Number: deterministic-floor MRR/answer_accuracy on rebaseline_500 before/after. (2) GROW the gold sets (#846->300, #820 proper-noun eval) so further parser/data wins are gate-admissible. (3) DEFER #863 LAS on ROI/hardness (attachment ambiguity = likely residue; can't reach store until the reparse pipeline exists) — NOT on measurability (LAS has ~2,700 aligned tokens of power; the ruler exists).
next: Set up the reparse wrapper (long-running -> user runs it) with the #823 junk filter folded in; measure rebaseline_500 deterministic floor before/after; then grow the gold sets.

method: Correlatives ending in -u/-a/-es project as DET only when their dependency role is determiner-like; nominal roles project as PRON.
limitation: This changes the UD scheme projection, not the native morphology or dependency tree. Prago and Cairo are development-informed frozen fixtures.

method: Native partiklo analyses project as ADV by default; the grammatical operators ajn, ĉi, and ĉu remain PART in the UD projection.
limitation: This changes only the UD POS projection. The three grammatical particle exceptions are a closed Esperanto function-word class; LAS/UAS and coverage are unchanged.

method: A narrow structural apposition rule handles comma-introduced noun phrases after pronouns or explicit articles and adjacent proper-noun renames, while preserving ordinary nominal sequences and address fragments.
limitation: Treebanks remain small and development-informed; punctuation-free common-noun apposition and semantic nominal ambiguity remain outside deterministic evidence.

method: Classify ol as a preposition and mark it as a non-clausal comparison only when its following span has no finite predicate; substantivized possessives such as ol via and ol la mia are treated as nominal PP complements.
limitation: The finite-clause distinction is structural; lexical and semantic comparison scope remains outside deterministic evidence.

metric: gold-head candidate recall / LAS_all / parse latency
method: Expose cycle-safe local heads within an eight-token window for every non-root content token without changing the selected dependency. Existing PP alternatives remain authoritative; new edges carry bounded-local structure provenance and are partial candidates.
limitation: This is candidate-generation evidence, not a quality improvement: LAS did not move and parse latency increased approximately 4x. The next selector must improve LAS or the bound must be narrowed/refined.

method: Structural candidate generation now preserves multiple relation labels licensed by accusative morphology and predicate head type, including obj/obl alternatives, while leaving the selected dependency unchanged.
limitation: This improves candidate representation only; LAS and UAS remain unchanged until a relation-aware graph selector is implemented.

metric: candidate-edge recall on LAS errors / theoretical candidate ceiling
method: Partition baseline LAS errors by whether the exact gold head-and-relation edge is already represented in the bounded candidate graph. The resulting ceiling assumes perfect global selection among represented edges and is an upper bound, not a parser score.
limitation: The partition measures candidate representation only; it does not establish that the represented edges can be selected jointly without cycles or regressions. A global constrained selector must beat the baseline LAS before runtime adoption.

metric: relation-level candidate-edge recall on LAS errors
method: Break down LAS errors with and without an exact candidate edge by gold dependency relation, exposing which relation families are ready for constrained selection and which still need candidate generation.
limitation: Relation-level counts do not establish that a selector can resolve the ambiguity; sentence-level global constraints and regression checks remain required.

method: Offline-only comparison of nearest and rightmost predicate heuristics over accusative nominal obj/obl alternatives, preserving every non-target dependency. All variants reduced LAS, so no runtime selector was merged.
limitation: The experiment is intentionally local and does not solve global predicate ownership, coordination, or cycle constraints; its negative result motivates a constrained global solver.

metric: gold-edge candidate recall / theoretical candidate ceiling
method: For nominative nouns, proper nouns, and pronouns, add nsubj alternatives to bounded local predicate candidates without changing the selected dependency. This is candidate-generation evidence only.
limitation: The rule raises the candidate ceiling but does not improve LAS until a global selector can choose among subject alternatives without regressions.

metric: LAS_all under global constrained beam decoder
method: Offline beam search over explicit attachment candidates with cycle rejection, baseline-edge prior, morphology-compatible subject/object relations, predicate-head preference, and object-slot penalties. No runtime integration after regression.
limitation: The decoder has structural constraints but no lexical valency or clause-aware predicate ownership model; its negative result is a scoring-design boundary, not evidence against global decoding.

metric: LAS_all under global decoder with suffix valency
method: Add deterministic Esperanto morphology signals to the offline global decoder: -iĝ penalizes object/oblique assignments and -ig favors direct objects. Runtime parser remains unchanged.
limitation: Suffix valency improves the decoder spike but does not overcome lexical frame ambiguity or clause ownership; the result remains below baseline LAS.

metric: LAS_all under global decoder with lexical valency
method: Use the versioned Apertium Esperanto lexicon for transitive/intransitive predicate-frame signals, retain morphology signals, and always include the baseline edge as a decoder fallback. Decode jointly with cycle and object-slot constraints.
limitation: The positive movement is only two Prago edges and the decoder remains offline; lexical frames cover only entries present in the Apertium snapshot and require broader clause/coordination constraints before runtime adoption.
